new_statements.quote: Remarque 1. Le gbanu et le 'bokoto sont en a3 par défaut, ces langues n'ayant pas de CVC à consonne finale occlusive. Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). new_statements.translation: Remark 1. Gbanu and 'Bokoto are in a3 by default, these languages having no CVC with a final stop. Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, one must answer in the negative: none of them presently shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again diachronically, in the interpretation of the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 190:] Gbanu is a language with two level tones and two contour tones, all attested on isolated CV.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gbanu is a two-level-tone language (plus rising and falling contours; verbs carry only grammatical TAM tone); the author, on the basis of his own fieldwork on Gbanu and 20 other Gbaya varieties, states that none of these languages has any accent (stress), intensity prominence or length phenomenon; the phonological system given for Gbanu (p. 185) contains consonants, vowels, syllable types and tones only.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None (no accent of any kind posited).
new_statements.exceptions: None synchronically; p. 345 entertains an accent only as a hypothesis for a pre-proto-Gbaya stage ('L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution').
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word/lexical prosodic system of the present-day languages (accent, intensity, length all denied); tone realisation in phrases (downdrift, up to five phonetic levels) is described separately on p. 190. The denial is made for all 21 varieties jointly in the contrastive recapitulation, with Gbanu explicitly among them (Remarque 1, same table); the Gbanu-specific chapter (pp. 184-200, based on 1973 Bossembélé fieldwork, 1100 words + 360 sentences) presents tones only and no accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's Gbanu data are from Nuclear Gbanu of Bossembélé (nucl1363; surveys also at Boyungene toward Boali and Bongbala toward Yaloké, reported as very homogeneous). The no-accent statement (p. 285) is made jointly for all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka varieties he surveyed, Gbanu explicitly included. The unread 2011/2019 works describe the Gbagiri dialect (gbag1253) of Yaloké.

sources.note: First-hand description (author's own Gbanu fieldwork 1970, 1971, 1973 at Bossembélé, p. 185). Ch. 10 'Phonologie du gbanu' gives consonants, vowels, syllable structures and tones (2 level + 2 contour tones, p. 185, 190) with no accent in the system; p. 285 Remarque 2 (contrastive recapitulation over all 21 varieties, Gbanu named in Remarque 1 of the same table) states explicitly that none of the languages presently has any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length; p. 345 Remarque repeats 'l'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles'.
